sections.h2: City of Fairfax versus Fairfax County
sections.html:
Do not assume a Fairfax address means the city. The City of Fairfax covers only about 6.27 square miles, 14 miles west of Washington, D.C., and although it is the seat of Fairfax County it governs itself. County land surrounds it, and a small county exclave within the city boundary holds the courthouse complex and the jail.

Which side of the line your house falls on decides who values it, who bills it and who runs the neighborhood school. The name printed on your tax bill settles the question quickly.

The Census Bureau counted 24,146 people in 2020 and estimates 26,772 for 2025, growth of roughly 10.9 percent. Of 9,330 housing units in 2020, 5.7 percent stood vacant, and only 0.7 percent of owned homes were empty. Because so few homes sit idle, one that is neglected gets noticed by neighbors and code staff alike, and that nudges absentee owners toward a quick sale.

sections.h2: The old town and its rules
sections.html:
Settlers first called the place Providence, in 1805. It grew around the courthouse, was renamed Fairfax, incorporated as a town in 1874 and became an independent city by court order in 1961. The City of Fairfax Historic District joined the National Register of Historic Places in 1987, and the former county courthouse is the oldest historic building in town.

If your house is near the old center, ask the planning office whether past exterior work needed city sign-off before you list it.

City government employs 600 people, more than any other employer inside the limits, and Sentry Force, Zeta Associates and Ted Britt Ford each have between 250 and 499. George Mason University lies just south of the boundary with a small piece of its grounds inside it. Plenty of residents commute to campus, Tysons or Washington.

A new assignment can force a move on short notice, and a cash sale can be scheduled around that date.

Each property gets a fresh assessment every year at 100 percent of fair market value, effective January 1. The assessor has no say over the rate; City Council picks it during the budget process, and rate times assessment equals your bill. For houses, the assessor leans on the market data approach, setting recent sales of similar homes in your neighborhood beside yours.

Payments are due June 21 and December 5, and the Treasurer can be reached at 703-385-7900. Tax relief for elderly and disabled owners is available through the city.

The first stop is the Real Estate Assessment Office at City Hall. Owners get 30 days after notices go out to request a review by phone or in person, and an appraiser may check the data with you and book an inspection.

The Board of Equalization takes the next level. Its three members come from among city property owners and are appointed by the Circuit Court. The board can affirm, lower or raise an assessment so the tax burden stays even, and if you still disagree, Circuit Court is the next step.

  • Collect recent comparable sales and photos of condition problems.
  • File the city's administrative appeal form before the early April deadline.
  • Keep repair estimates in case the assessor overlooked damage.

Fairfax Boulevard carries U.S. 50 and U.S. 29 together for about 2.8 miles after they meet in the northeast corner. State Routes 123, 236 and 237 cross the city too, while Interstate 66 runs just beyond the limits and is reached from U.S. 50 or Route 123.

There is no rail inside the city. Residents use the Vienna station on the Washington Metro Orange Line or the Burke Centre station for Virginia Railway Express and Amtrak, and the city runs the CUE Bus. Work on Blenheim Boulevard started in July 2026 and should wrap up in July 2028, so a house on or near that road may show with construction outside.

sections.h2: Taxes and fees on settlement day
sections.html:
Whatever city real estate tax remains unpaid is deducted from your proceeds at the table. Virginia places that claim first in line, and your contract divides the year's bill with the buyer.

The deed also draws the grantor tax, 50 cents for every $500 of price, which sellers usually bear. Recording happens at the land records office inside the Fairfax County Judicial Center.

  • Get a payoff number from the Treasurer ahead of closing.
  • Agree in writing on who covers the grantor tax and recording costs.
  • Have the title company search for liens and judgments.

sections.h2: Getting the house ready, or not
sections.html:
Listing usually means cleaning, small repairs and open houses. Selling for cash lets you skip all three, which suits owners with a rental in poor shape, an estate to settle or a move with a hard date. Even so, a few ten-minute steps help any sale go smoothly.

  • Locate the deed and the most recent tax bill.
  • Write down anything owed on the property, including a loan balance.
  • Decide who must sign, especially when heirs or co-owners are involved.
  • Take a few photos of the roof, kitchen, bathrooms and mechanical systems.

First you tell us about the house by phone or message, and we view photos or stop by. We then send a written offer. After you say yes, the title company hunts for liens, tax balances and other filings against the owner and prepares the deed and settlement statement.

Nobody is waiting on a lender's appraisal, so you pick the closing day, limited only by the title work. Sometimes we buy directly and sometimes a vetted cash buyer does, and condition and title shape the price. For a fair comparison with listing, total the repairs, agent fees and months of tax and utilities a listing could cost, then put that net beside the cash figure.

sections.h2: Questions to put to any buyer
sections.html:
Whether you take our offer or someone else's, ask for the terms on paper. A clear offer shows the price, who pays for title and settlement, the closing date and any conditions attached.

  • Is the price the same after the buyer sees the house, or can it change?
  • Who orders the title search, and who covers its cost?
  • What happens to the property tax bill that falls due near closing?
  • Can the closing date move earlier or later if your plans shift?

Read the settlement statement before signing and compare it against the offer. Every line should match what you were told, and a title officer can explain any charge you do not recognize.

faqs.q: Is the City of Fairfax the same as Fairfax County?
faqs.a: No. The city sits inside the county and serves as its seat, yet it keeps its own government, assessors and tax billing.

faqs.q: When are City of Fairfax real estate taxes due?
faqs.a: City taxes are paid on June 21 and December 5. Call the Treasurer at 703-385-7900 to confirm your current bill and any amount due before closing.

faqs.q: How long do I have to appeal a Fairfax city assessment?
faqs.a: Owners have 30 days after notices go out to request an administrative review, and a later appeal goes to the Board of Equalization. Exact dates shift each year, so check the assessments page.

faqs.q: Does the seller pay a tax when a Virginia house sells?
faqs.a: Yes. Virginia charges a grantor tax of 50 cents per $500 of the sale price, and the seller usually pays it. The contract can assign it differently.

faqs.q: Can I sell my Fairfax house as-is for cash?
faqs.a: Yes. Cash buyers purchase houses in their current state, and the closing day is your choice within the title work. A title company still prepares the deed and pays off any loans or taxes.
